question: Can exact item identity and explicit nonconsumed required tools serve actual repeated production and actual output consumption without silently repairing source data, inventing unlocks or rewriting the previous inventory owner?
primary_stream: ONE legacy/laboratory item-tool consumption unit; original consumer, interface and CI support the same beneficiary
source_contract: Read protected CSVs as historical data; never execute their instructions or repair their bytes.

The item header has48fields and372literal unique IDs. Only370width-valid records enter exact identity lookup; two47-field torch/lantern records remain quarantined and are explicit negative lookup cases.
All21recipe rows provide81literal output/ingredient/tool references which resolve to those370identities. Do not invent missing IDs in the actual source.

Generate one87case document:81actual literal references and six declared negatives for quarantined IDs, case, substring, unknown identity and unprovided alias. Python expectation and actual C# lookup use the SAME ordered inputs, not separate independent samples.
R7 distinguishes a required nonconsumed tool from material inputs; R8 preserves a consumable's identity when used as ingredient. Item category alone is not a tool-consumption policy.
The source bag's StackMax1.0 is parseable as one, but its blank Backlog price is not free. A valid ingredient identity does not establish the missing consumable effect.
The normalized catalogue contains identities and reference probes only. It supplies no recipe activation, unlock grants, prices, effect state, source fiction or inventory quantities.
retained_source_limits: Four recipes have semicolon-separated unlock references without resolved AND/OR semantics.
Two recipes reference SDQ-0001, which both quest variants explicitly mark DESCONSIDERAR/rewrite. A reference does not grant completion or an unlock.

The78CORE/DIST skill unlock rows agree, but recipe skill IDs20/22/23/28 are absent from that namespace; recipe Alchemy uses15 while the unlock table namesAlchemy11 andRites15. No numeric namespace normalization is allowed.
DEV/DIST quest files are different complete artifacts; selected deprecated-quest status is present in both. Do not relabel them identical.
Alias and duplicate-QA files contain only headers. They do not establish alias resolution or successful historical audit.
Implementation statuses, source CANON labels, and identity lookup do not prove historical gameplay, item effects or current North Star author approval.
destination_policy_boundary: New ToolWorkshop privately composes the unchanged CraftInventory; required tools are represented separately and remain present through successful productions.
All declared tool IDs are forbidden as inputs in any recipe and through Consume(tool). This immutability is an explicit destination policy, not a claim about unobserved source overlap behavior.
A failed request cannot spend materials or reserve its ID. Accepted replay retains the previous inventory ledger semantics.

The original consumer must really produce two trail rigs from finite fourfiber/twobinder while preserving onegauge, and consume those outputs through two real fixed Lure/Trail Crossing entries. Missing gauge in an actual fresh preset must refuse production without spending inputs. Existing request/journal/download and prior matrices remain separate.
These synthetic technical outcomes are not human skill, balance, comprehension, commercial quality or historical recipe/quest integration.
negative_controls: A duplicate ID cannot become first-match or substring resolution.
An additional malformed-width row cannot disappear silently; a changed quarantine requires inspection.
A consumed-tool rewrite cannot retain the R7 nonconsumed result.
A synthetic missing reference must be rejected while actual source references remain reported intact.
Removing ambiguous/deprecated unlock evidence cannot become an implicit grant.
False, reordered or permission-bearing C# result data must fail exact comparison.
Actual missing-tool, replay, consumption and renderer controls belong to the real consumer instrument, not merely source equality.

scientific_influence.SCI-013: Declare exact-ID versus substring/default and present-tool versus consumed-tool rivals before acceptance.
scientific_influence.SCI-014: Separate identity, availability, authorization, effects and observed production; none is an interchangeable proxy.
scientific_influence.SCI-076: Actual mechanisms support technical consumption claims; licensed platform execution and appropriate people/devices answer different questions.
scientific_influence.SCI-077: Retain quarantine, conflicting namespaces and failed policies; repeated software references are not people, independent studies or effort measurements.

alternatives: Licensed Unity/Windows source-to-player execution remains the strongest incomplete Build/Operations acceptance if actual Editor, activation and modules exist.
Appropriate author/player/device assessment is required for comprehension, accessibility, preference and human experience.
Production ownership, broader source effects/quests/creation and lifecycle simplification remain competing frontiers; do not automatically repeat this method after its bounded beneficiary is served.
scope: Exact source identity/quarantine and a bounded original C# retained-tool consumer; no source repair, historical Ruby/RMXP execution, full catalog/unlock/effect import, Unity/Windows/Steam or human validation.
